title: Blooming · Psychology and coaching practice – career coaching and therapy for people living in Italy
description: Career coaching and guidance, workplace coaching, psychological support and psychotherapy for people living in Italy or about to move here. Online. Free 30-minute first meeting.

data.title: Work and life don't run on separate tracks.
data.subtitle: Least of all when you've moved to Italy. So here, career support and therapy sit side by side.

p.t: Career coaching and guidance, workplace coaching, psychological support and psychotherapy, for people living in Italy or about to move here. Online, from anywhere in Italy, or before you've even arrived.

data.title: Work, settling in and hard times often come together.

p.t: You had a career before Italy. Here your CV doesn't get you a single interview, your qualifications don't count the way you expected, and everyone tells you it's who you know. Or you've found work, but the way things are done here wears you down.
You're not the only one: 42% of expats in Italy rate the local job market negatively.

The psychologist who guides your career has worked in HR for over ten years, in recruitment, training and change management, and knows the Italian job market. She'll be straight with you about what you can realistically aim for and how much your Italian matters. Nobody can promise you a job, and she won't. Together you build a concrete strategy. If there's more going on than work, she'll notice, and if you want, she can suggest working on it with one of our psychotherapists too.

items.title: When settling in takes longer than you expected

p.t: You came for a job, for love or for a fresh start. Perhaps you followed your partner and left your own work behind. The paperwork is exhausting, and we can't do it for you. Making friends takes longer than anyone told you, and getting by in Italian all day can feel isolating and demoralising.
Nearly half of expats in Italy (45%) say making local friends is hard.
Career guidance helps you rebuild your working life here. Psychological support helps with the loneliness and the homesickness.

items.title: When you're going through a hard time, far from home

p.t: Anxiety that won't let go, or a loss. A separation. A baby on the way, or one that hasn't come. A parent who is ill in another country. Or something you can't put into words yet, except that you don't feel like yourself.
Here you work with a psychologist and psychotherapist. You don't have to explain from scratch how things work here.

data.title: Coaching, psychological support and psychotherapy do different jobs.

p.t: For making decisions about work and acting on them.
For getting through a hard time, sometimes in just a few sessions.
When the difficulty runs deep or has lasted a long time.
A problem at work doesn't automatically call for therapy. In the first meeting we work out together what kind of help fits.

data.title: The first meeting is free, takes 30 minutes, and there's no obligation to continue.

p.t: Finding a professional who really works in English can feel like looking for a needle in a haystack. In 30 free minutes you can find out whether we're the right fit.
Pick what you need and a time. Not sure? Pick "Not sure yet": in the first meeting we work out together which path to take.
On a video call you tell us what's going on, and you find out whether we can help and how we'd work. It isn't a session, and nobody will push you to continue.
If you'd like to go on, you plan the next steps with her. If it doesn't feel right, you can switch to someone else or stop there. If you decide not to go on, we won't contact you again.

data.title: Often, what weighs on people starts at work.

p.t: A manager who never listens. A conflict in the team that nobody tackles. We can help one person cope, but it's better to deal with things where they start. That's why we also work with organisations that want a healthier workplace culture.

To bloom is to come through a hard time, find your own resources again and feel well again, in your own time. That's why our logo is a lotus with the Greek letter Ψ, the symbol of psychology, inside it. It's what we want to make possible for the people who come to us.
